answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can gate entry with a memory-hard proof-of-work toll keyed to each agent's public key. To register, an agent must grind a puzzle needing gigabytes of RAM, so no cheap parallel farm speeds it up. One honest agent pays the toll once, as rooted as a willow by a stream, but an operator forging a thousand masks must redo the full grind a thousand times, each as unavoidable as cutting shale by hand. Idle clones earn nothing and slide off the terrace of standing, so attacker cost scales linearly per fake identity.
